claims.text: The Talent Development Awards are available to promote the acquisition and advancement of skills in relevant areas.
The awards are for UK-based researchers.
The awards support innovative research methods through skills development, collaboration, or dissemination.
The scheme aims to enable researchers to build skills and capacities to develop current and future research.
The scheme is open for applications.
The scheme opened for applications on July 15, 2026.
The deadline for applications is October 7, 2026, at 17:00 BST.
Awards can start as early as March 1, 2027.
Awards have a duration of a minimum of six months and a maximum of 12 months.
The British Academy has been funded by the UK government, Department for Science, Innovation and Technology (DSIT) for this scheme.
The scheme includes core areas like quantitative skills, data science, digital humanities, and languages.
The scheme is designed for researchers who wish to adopt an interdisciplinary approach.
The scheme provides early career researchers with opportunities to develop specialist skills.
The scheme offers mid and senior career researchers opportunities to diversify their skills and methodological approaches.
The scheme encourages researchers to champion their newly acquired skills within their wider community.
The overarching aims of the scheme are to invest in UK talent and skills.
The scheme aims to raise the quality of advanced quantitative skills and/or data science skills used in research.
The scheme aims to create new opportunities for knowledge and skills exchange across disciplines and sectors.
The scheme aims to promote language learning and the transferable skills it provides.
The scheme is intended for established researchers in the humanities and social sciences.
Eligible applicants must have a current long-term appointment at a UK-based Higher Education Institution (HEI) or Independent Research Organisation (IRO).
Applicants must be intending to pursue original, independent research within the Humanities or Social Sciences.
Independent researchers without an institutional affiliation are not eligible to apply.
Co-applicants may be based in the UK or overseas.
The maximum grant amount is £10,000.
Awards are not intended as time buy-out for the award-holder.
Awards are not offered on a Full Economic Costing (FEC) basis.
100 per cent of the awarded funds must be used solely for the purposes outlined in the application and agreed in the award letter.
Awards are expected to commence no later than March 31, 2027.
